---
title: "Labs and activities"
subtitle: "Apply an idea, produce a small artifact, and make your reasoning visible"
---

Labs and activities are short exercises that make the course ideas concrete. Each page explains how you may collaborate and what to submit.

## Week 1

- [Activity 1 — What tool fits the job?](week-01-tool-choice-discussion.qmd): discuss when a spreadsheet, plain file, database, program, or combination best fits a situation. [Answer key](week-01-tool-choice-discussion-answer-key.qmd).
- [Lab 1 — Make the file fail on purpose](week-01-file-representation-lab.qmd): expose the assumptions and failure modes hidden in a convenient flat file, then propose a first relational model. [Answer key](week-01-file-representation-lab-answer-key.qmd).

## Week 2

- [Activity 2 — Relations and keys](week-02-relations-and-keys.qmd): write relation schemas, identify superkeys and candidate keys, choose primary keys, locate foreign keys, and reason about checking uniqueness in a relation instance. [Answer key](week-02-relations-and-keys-answer-key.qmd).

## Week 4

- [Activity 3 — Design an escape-room database](week-04-escape-room-schema.qmd): write three related tables, practice `ALTER TABLE`, then compare and discuss your schema with classmates.

## Week 6

- [Lab 2 — Follow the save](week-03-query-reasoning-lab.qmd): practice selection and joins with video game saves, games, and players, then check the connections in a query result. Group work is welcome; each student submits their own Word document.

## Week 7

- [Activity 4 — ER relationships](week-07-er-relationship-practice.qmd): distinguish entities, attributes, and relationships; compare cardinalities across four scenarios; draw a combined ER diagram; and explain relationship attributes and participation. Approximately 40–45 minutes. Work individually or in a group, then compare with classmates.

## Submission principle

Lab submissions are deliberately small. They should preserve enough reasoning that the instructor can see what you tried, what you concluded, and which assumptions remain unresolved. The detailed submission location and deadline will be announced with each offering.
